As a Senior CUDA DSP Engineer , you will port our 5G positioning signal-processing algorithms from CPU reference implementations to high-throughput, low-latency CUDA implementations on NVIDIA GPUs. You will work closely with signal-processing domain experts to meet real-time latency targets, maximise memory-bandwidth utilisation, and maintain strict numerical parity with the algorithm prototypes. The work is hands-on kernel development, library integration, and performance validation.
 Responsibilities: 
Port existing signal processing algorithms to high-throughput, low-latency CUDA GPU implementations.
Write, test, and tune custom CUDA C/C++ kernels using shared memory, registers, warp shuffles, and asynchronous copy primitives.
Replace CPU library calls (Intel MKL and IPP) with NVIDIA math and signal processing libraries including cuFFT, cuBLAS, cuSignal, and NPP.
Implement asynchronous processing pipelines using CUDA streams and pinned host memory to overlap PCIe data transfers with compute.
Design unit and integration test suites that verify functional equivalence between reference and GPU pipeline outputs.
Maintain clear architectural documentation and collaborate with domain engineering teams.
 Your profile: 
 4+ years of professional C/C++ development experience, including 3+ years writing low-level CUDA applications for NVIDIA GPUs.
High proficiency in C multithreading and low-level memory management.
Working knowledge of core DSP concepts, including FFT, MUSIC, and parameter estimation.
 Hands-on experience identifying hardware bottlenecks using Nsight Systems and Nsight
Compute.
Based in the US or Europe, with working hours that overlap with our engineering teams in Romania and the US.
M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related field.
Experience with Intel vector intrinsics (AVX2, AVX-512), Intel IPP, or Intel MKL.
Familiarity with Python wrappers for GPU acceleration such as PyCUDA, CuPy, or RAPIDS cuSignal.
Background in parameter estimation, geolocation, software-defined radio, or 5G
 telecommunications.
